Build a deep overview of the project done so far.

THings I want:
- separate the database engine from the database, as in we should be able to pull out databases out of leandb
- Host the bases, operations we are getting an API on top of them, being able to query data, run migrations (also think how to run typed migrations) 
- I think each base should be Lean package, with 3 things, types, instances of the types (stored in sql), and queries, the migration should bump the version, and the engine should tell which migrations will have impact etc etc, because we are using sqlite, we can also have full backups, to allow easy rolldown of migrations if need be, so the base can multiple migration, and a live version. Cna probably do migratiions usng LeanMeta programming, IDK, but I want to be able to import the base lean packaage and use it in other projects for easy access of types (and data and queries) in other projects, you might need to think serializaiton, IDK, ultrathink write a plan

1	# LeanDB
2	
3	**Strongly typed SQL in Lean 4.** LeanDB combines Lean's expressive type
4	system with SQLite, giving a dependently typed front end to a SQL backend.
5	That gives you:
6	
7	- validated, typed data,
8	- queries checked against the tables they read, and
9	- schema-derived migrations (with typed data transformations coming soon).
10	
11	## Typed Data
12	
13	Model domain values directly. Every value read from SQLite or decoded from
14	JSON passes through its `ColCodec`, while `Ref User` makes a foreign key's
15	target part of its Lean type.
16	
17	```lean
18	import LeanDb
19	
20	open LeanDb
21	
22	structure Title where
23	  raw : String
24	  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Ord
25	
26	def Title.make (s : String) : Except String Title :=
27	  let title := s.trimAscii.toString
28	  if title.isEmpty then .error "title must be nonempty" else .ok ⟨title⟩
29	
30	instance : ColCodec Title := ColCodec.via (·.raw) Title.make
31	
32	inductive Status where
33	  | backlog | inProgress | done
34	  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Ord, LeanDb.ClosedEnum
35	
36	structure User where
37	  name : String
38	  deriving Repr, LeanDb.Entity
39	
40	structure Ticket where
41	  title    : Title
42	  status   : Status := .backlog
43	  reporter : Ref User
44	  deriving Repr, LeanDb.Entity
45	
46	def schema : List TableSpec :=
47	  [Entity.spec User, Entity.spec Ticket]
48	```
49	
50	`deriving LeanDb.Entity` produces each table specification; `schema` lists
51	those tables in foreign-key dependency order. LeanDB derives the columns,
52	default, foreign-key constraint, JSON codec, and migration metadata from the
53	entity declarations, so there is no second schema to keep in sync.
54	
55	## Typed Queries
56	
57	The table list fixes the predicate's input type, so a predicate for the wrong
58	table does not compile. This join is checked in Lean and runs as one SQL
59	statement:
60	
61	```lean
62	def activeTickets : DbM (Array (Stored Ticket × Stored User)) :=
63	  select [Ticket, User]
64	    (fun (ticket, user) =>
65	      ticket.val.reporter == user.ref && ticket.val.status != .done)
66	    (.key fun (ticket, _) => ticket.val.title)
67	
68	-- `select [User]` requires a `Stored User → Bool`, so this is rejected:
69	#check_failure
70	  select [User] (fun (ticket : Stored Ticket) => ticket.val.status == .done)
71	```
72	
73	LeanDB reifies the part of the predicate it can express in SQL and always
74	checks the original Lean predicate on the returned rows, preserving Lean's
75	reference semantics.
76	
77	## Schema migrations (typed transformations coming soon)
78	
79	A migration starts as a type-safe schema edit. For example, adding an optional
80	field is enough to produce a non-destructive migration plan:
81	
82	```diff
83	 structure Ticket where
84	   title    : Title
85	   status   : Status := .backlog
86	   reporter : Ref User
87	+  assignee : Option (Ref User)
88	   deriving Repr, LeanDb.Entity
89	```
90	
91	```console
92	$ tickets migrate status
93	{"destructive":false,"notes":[],"ok":true,"steps":["add column \"ticket\".\"assignee\""]}
94	
95	$ tickets migrate apply
96	{"applied":["add column \"ticket\".\"assignee\""],"ok":true,…}
97	```
98	
99	LeanDB already derives and transactionally applies schema changes. A future
100	typed-transformation API will cover changes that need application-specific
101	row conversion rather than a mechanical SQLite migration.
102	
103	Backed by SQLite ([leansqlite](https://github.com/leanprover/leansqlite),
104	bundled — nothing to install). Machine-first: every command emits one JSON
105	value; errors are typed with stable codes; exit codes mean things.
106	
107	## Setup
108	
109	You need [`elan`](https://github.com/leanprover/elan) (the Lean toolchain
110	manager). Then:
111	
112	```bash
113	git clone https://github.com/theoriclabs/LeanDB.git leandb && cd leandb
114	lake build            # engine (first build compiles bundled SQLite; takes a few minutes)
115	lake build leandb     # the importer executable (used in "Importing" below)
116	lake build leandb_tests && .lake/build/bin/leandb_tests   # optional: "all engine tests passed"
117	```
118	
119	Maintainers can run the full engine, example, and importer release pass with
120	`./scripts/release_check.sh`; see `RELEASING.md` for the tag checklist.
121	
122	## A new base from scratch
123	
124	A LeanDB database ("base") is an ordinary Lake package depending on
125	`leandb`. Three files. Make a directory anywhere and add:
126	
127	**`lean-toolchain`** — must match the engine's (copy it):
128	
129	```
130	leanprover/lean4:v4.33.0
131	```
132	
133	**`lakefile.toml`**:
134	
135	```toml
136	name = "notes"
137	defaultTargets = ["notes"]
138	
139	[[require]]
140	name = "leandb"
141	path = "/absolute/path/to/leandb"   # or a relative path
142	
143	[[lean_exe]]
144	name = "notes"
145	root = "Main"
146	```
147	
148	**`Main.lean`** — a complete base in one file:
149	
150	```lean
151	import LeanDb
152	
153	open LeanDb LeanDb.Cli
154	
155	/-- A validated newtype: database and JSON decoding use its smart constructor. -/
156	structure Title where
157	  raw : String
158	  deriving Repr
159	
160	def Title.make (s : String) : Except String Title :=
161	  let t := s.trimAscii.toString
162	  if t.isEmpty then .error "title must be nonempty" else .ok ⟨t⟩
163	
164	instance : ColCodec Title := ColCodec.via (·.raw) Title.make
165	
166	/-- A closed world: these are ALL the statuses. Stored as TEXT with a
167	    CHECK constraint; not an entity — you cannot insert or delete one. -/
168	inductive Status where
169	  | draft | published
170	  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Ord, LeanDb.ClosedEnum
171	
172	structure Note where
173	  title  : Title
174	  body   : String
175	  status : Status := .draft
176	  deriving Repr, LeanDb.Entity
177	
178	def schema : List TableSpec := [Entity.spec Note]
179	
180	/-- Domain logic the query compiler may unfold into SQL. -/
181	@[db] def Note.isDraft (n : Note) : Bool := n.status == .draft
182	
183	def drafts : DbM (Array (Stored Note)) :=
184	  select [Note] (fun n => n.val.isDraft) (.key (·.val.title.raw))
185	
186	open Lean (Json) in
187	def main (args : List String) : IO UInt32 :=
188	  Cli.run {
189	    name := "notes"
190	    dbPath := "data" / "notes.sqlite"
191	    specs := schema
192	    tables := [.of Note]
193	    queries := [query% drafts]   -- CLI arity/parsing derived from the def's signature
194	  } args
195	```
196	
197	Build and use (the instance file is created on first touch):
198	
199	```bash
200	lake build
201	notes=./.lake/build/bin/notes
202	
203	$ $notes insert note '{"title":"  First  ","body":"hello"}'
204	{"ok":true,"row":{"body":"hello","id":1,"status":"draft","title":"First"}}
205	#         title trimmed by the smart constructor ─┘        └─ default filled in
206	
207	$ $notes insert note '{"title":"   ","body":"no"}'
208	{"code":"decode","message":"note.title: title must be nonempty","ok":false}   # exit 2
209	
210	$ $notes query drafts
211	{"ok":true,"result":[{"body":"hello","id":1,"status":"draft","title":"First"}]}
212	
213	$ $notes version
214	{"code_fingerprint":"…","in_sync":true,"instance_fingerprint":"…","ok":true,"schema_version":1}
215	```
216	
217	## Changing the schema — migrations
218	
219	The schema is the code, so a migration starts with an edit. Add a variant
220	to the closed world and a new field:
221	
222	```lean
223	inductive Status where
224	  | draft | published | archived      -- grew the world
225	  ...
226	structure Note where
227	  title  : Title
228	  body   : String
229	  status : Status := .draft
230	  pinned : Option Bool                -- new column: Option, or give it a default
231	  ...
232	```
233	
234	`lake build`, then watch the instance refuse to lie about what it holds:
235	
236	```bash
237	$ $notes rows note
238	{"code":"schema_mismatch","message":"schema fingerprint mismatch: …","ok":false}   # exit 4
239	
240	$ $notes migrate status
241	{"destructive":false,"notes":["\"note\".\"status\" changed shape → table rebuild"],
242	 "ok":true,"steps":["rebuild table \"note\" (copying 3 columns)"]}
243	
244	$ $notes migrate apply
245	{"applied":["rebuild table \"note\" (copying 3 columns)"],"fingerprint":"…","ok":true,…}
246	
247	$ $notes rows note --eq status=draft
248	{"count":1,"ok":true,"rows":[{"body":"hello","id":1,"pinned":null,"status":"draft","title":"First"}]}
249	
250	$ $notes version
251	{…,"in_sync":true,"schema_version":2}
252	```
253	
254	The rules, all loud:
255	
256	- **New columns must be `Option` or carry a `:= default`** — a declared
257	  default backfills existing rows (and shows up in the DDL and the
258	  `schema` output); without one, a `NOT NULL` addition is refused with
259	  guidance rather than inventing a value.
260	- **New tables** apply as plain `CREATE TABLE`.
261	- **Changed column shapes** (a grown/renamed closed world, a type change)
262	  rebuild the table in place, copying surviving columns. **Shrinking a
263	  closed world** with rows still using the removed variant fails the new
264	  CHECK during the copy and **rolls back** — vocabulary shrinks only when
265	  the data already conforms.
266	- **Dropping tables or columns** is refused unless you pass
267	  `migrate apply --allow-destructive`.
268	- Everything runs in one transaction with a foreign-key check before
269	  commit; each apply is journaled in `_leandb_migrations` and bumps
270	  `schema_version`.
271	
272	## Importing an existing SQLite database
273	
274	Point the importer at any SQLite file; it generates a complete typed base:
275	
276	```bash
277	$ leandb import-sqlite inventory.db --name inventory --out ./inventory \
278	    --require-path /absolute/path/to/leandb
279	{"imported":["vendors","parts"],"skipped":[],…}
280	
281	$ cd inventory && mkdir -p data && cp ../inventory.db data/   # adopt the file
282	$ lake build
283	$ ./.lake/build/bin/inventory rows parts --eq vendor_id=1
284	{"count":1,"ok":true,"rows":[{"id":1,"label":"sprocket","qty":12,"vendor_id":1}]}
285	```
286	
287	What you get: `INTEGER` → `Int64`, FKs → `Ref <Table>`, nullable →
288	`Option`, and **every TEXT column becomes its own named newtype with an
289	identity smart constructor** — *import loose, tighten forever*: the base
290	is never stringly, and each future validation is one `make` function away
291	(followed by the ordinary migration flow above). Everything that can't be
292	carried — views, triggers, composite-key tables, BLOB columns — is listed
293	**by name** with a reason in the generated `IMPORT.md` /
294	`import-report.json`. Silent partiality is forbidden.
295	
296	The adopted file keeps working with plain `sqlite3` the whole time; LeanDB
297	adds its `_leandb_*` bookkeeping tables on first open.
298	
299	## The CLI every base gets
300	
301	`Cli.run` derives the whole surface from your entity list:
302	
303	| Command | Meaning |
304	|---|---|
305	| `schema` | schema as JSON, derived from the types (closed worlds visible) |
306	| `version` | code vs instance fingerprint, `schema_version`, `in_sync` |
307	| `insert <table> <json>` | decode through the smart constructors; defaults fill omitted fields |
308	| `get <table> <id>` · `delete <table> <id>` | typed row ops; `delete` of a referenced row → `restricted` |
309	| `update <table> <id> <partial-json>` | column-level merge, re-validated, written compare-and-swap |
310	| `rows <table> [--eq col=value]… [--limit n]` | conjunctive equality filters — the CLI's whole filter language, by design |
311	| `query <name> [args…]` | your `query%`-registered queries; args parse by type |
312	| `migrate status` / `migrate apply [--allow-destructive]` | see above |
313	| `log [n]` | the query log: verb, reified SQL plan, outcome, row count |
314	| `serve` | JSON-lines over stdio on one persistent connection (each request is a JSON argv array) |
315	
316	Exit codes: `0` ok · `2` typed `DbError` (JSON on stderr, `code` field:
317	`decode`, `not_found`, `stale`, `restricted`, `missing_ref`, `duplicate`, `schema`, `enum_drift`,
318	`migrate`, `sqlite`) · `3` usage · `4` schema/version mismatch.
319	
320	## Queries are Lean
321	
322	`select` takes a plain lambda; the four verbs are all there is:
323	
324	```lean
325	insert Ticket {...}         -- : DbM (Stored Ticket), returns assigned id
326	update old new              -- compare-and-swap: a lost race is .stale, never a clobber
327	delete someId               -- referenced row → .restricted
328	select [Ticket, User] (fun (t, u) => t.val.reporter == u.ref && t.val.priority == .p0)
329	  (.andThen (.key fun (t, _) => t.val.createdAt) (.desc (.key fun (_, u) => u.val.handle)))
330	```
331	
332	At each call site an elaboration tactic reifies the predicate into a plan:
333	column/value comparisons (captured variables become bound SQL parameters),
334	joins, `&&`/`||`/`!`, `Option` null tests, `@[db]` helpers unfolded — and a
335	`match` on a closed world compiles to SQL by case-splitting it (the gpus
336	example's `Chip.vendor c == .amd`, a seven-constructor match, executes as
337	`chip IS 'mi300x' OR chip IS 'mi325x'`). Whatever the tactic can't
338	translate stays a *residual* conjunct: the lambda is **always** applied to
339	what comes back, so plans narrow fetches but can never change results.
340	`log` shows exactly what was pushed; `set_option leandb.explain true`
341	shows plans at compile time.
342	
343	## Example bases
344	
345	The hand-written bases are standalone packages with tests and a
346	`CLI_TRANSCRIPT.md`; `legacy` is the checked-in importer output:
347	
348	| Base | Domain | Worth seeing |
349	|---|---|---|
350	| `examples/tickets` | issue tracker | SLA join, `@[db]` helpers, the reference base |
351	| `examples/crm` | companies/people/asks | pipeline join, keyword enum variant `«open»` |
352	| `examples/shop` | ecommerce | basket/revenue joins, Money/Sku/Qty scalars |
353	| `examples/gpus` | GPU SKUs & providers | match→CASE pushdown; `#check_failure LeanDb.delete (α := Chip) ⟨1⟩` — you can't delete a chip from the universe |
354	| `examples/gpumarket` | GPU rental market + models | providers as a *closed world* (deleting Lambda doesn't typecheck), total vocabulary functions, `query h100 onDemand` → cheapest first, `canServe <model>` joins models against listings |
355	| `examples/pricewatch` | ecommerce price comparison | typed hard constraints plus sorted, Pareto-front, and knee-point selection strategies |
356	| `examples/legacy` | generated by `import-sqlite` | what the importer emits |
357	
358	```bash
359	cd examples/tickets && lake build tickets
360	./.lake/build/bin/tickets query seed
361	./.lake/build/bin/tickets query slaBreached 1700000000
362	./.lake/build/bin/tickets log 3
363	```
364	
365	## Repo map
366	
367	```text
368	LeanDb/Core.lean     Id/Ref/Stored, Col, ColCodec, ClosedEnum, ColumnSpec, DbError
369	LeanDb/Entity.lean   Entity class, TableSpec, DDL generation, fingerprint
370	LeanDb/Derive.lean   deriving LeanDb.Entity / LeanDb.ClosedEnum (incl. field defaults)
371	LeanDb/Select.lean   Rows ts, SortBy, RowsOf, selectSpec (the reference semantics)
372	LeanDb/Pred.lean     typed plan IR (Pred)  LeanDb/PlanElab.lean  the leandb_plan tactic, @[db]
373	LeanDb/Db.lean       DbM, the four verbs, joined executor, open checks, query log
374	LeanDb/Migrate.lean  schema diff → steps, transactional apply, journal
375	LeanDb/Json.lean     schema/row/error JSON, merge decode   LeanDb/Cli.lean  the CLI driver
376	LeanDb/CliQuery.lean query%                LeanDb/Import.lean  import-sqlite generator
377	Tests.lean           engine tests          Main.lean            the leandb executable
378	```
379	
380	Design docs: [`plan.md`](plan.md) (interface spec),
381	[`plan-v2.md`](plan-v2.md) (milestones and status),

1	# LeanDB roadmap
2	
3	**2026-09-01.** From v0.2.0. Companion to `plan-v2.md` (what was built and
4	why) and `proposals/` (what is designed). This file is the order of work
5	and the acceptance test for each step; it is updated as steps land.
6	
7	The discipline is unchanged from plan-v2: *correctness machinery first,
8	optimization machinery only when a test demands it.* Concretely — every
9	engine change below is preceded by a base that already exists and already
10	has the query that needs it.
11	
12	| Step | Milestone | Status |
13	|---|---|---|
14	| R0 | Land the verified 0.2.x fixes and the design documents | done 2026-09-01 |
15	| R1 | `examples/eats` — restaurant base, plus the captured-parameter case split | done 2026-09-01 |
16	| R2 | `examples/kernels` — kernel base, evidence for nested values | done 2026-09-01 |
17	| R3 | LEP-0002 — typed predicate IR | done 2026-09-01 |
18	| R4 | LEP-0003 nested values · LEP-0004 child-table quantifiers | done 2026-09-01 |

22	
23	## R0 — Land what is verified
24	
25	Four defects fixed and green under `scripts/release_check.sh` (pushdown
26	through newtype projections; BLOB as a typed `decode`; importer
27	not-carried precision; hardened constraint classification), plus
28	LEP-0002 and the stress-domain study.
29	
30	**Done when:** committed on `main`, release check passing.
31	
32	## R1 — Restaurant base (`examples/eats`)
33	
34	The base from study §2, built against the engine *as it is*. It exercises
35	the largest share of what exists — closed worlds with total functions,
36	ordering through validated newtypes, `||`/`if` on columns for the
37	midnight wrap, three-table joins, `Option (Ref _)` — and exposes exactly
38	one missing thing in its central query.
39	
40	Included three small engine changes the base needed, each with goldens:
41	**case-splitting on a captured closed-enum parameter** (study §3.4 — a
42	`@[db]` function matching on its parameter first no longer goes
43	residual); **folding value/value guards at plan build** (`cmpVVS`: the
44	guards a parameter split leaves are decidable once the parameter is
45	known, so the tree collapses to the surviving column conditions — both
46	match orders of `Diet.allows` yield the same SQL); and **`if`/`cond` on
47	columns** as `(c ∧ t) ∨ (¬c ∧ e)`, which the study assumed and the tactic
48	lacked. Also `rows --eq` now splits at the first `=` only, found by R2.

54	- `eats log` shows `residual conjuncts: 0` for `openFor` and for the

61	  first pushes with residual 0; end-to-end differential equal to
62	  `selectUnplanned`.
63	- Added to `release_check.sh`.
64	
65	## R2 — Kernel base (`examples/kernels`)
66	
67	The base from study §1. Its job is to make the nested-values decision
68	concrete: `KernelSig` stored as a JSON-codec'd column (opaque to SQL) with
69	denormalized search columns, `Prog ins outs` and composition entirely in
70	Lean, `Bench.sku` from gpumarket's `Gpu` (first cross-base type reuse).
71	
72	**Done when:**
73	- `Prog.seq` of a kernel whose output dtype does not match the next
74	  kernel's input is a `#check_failure` — typed composition, demonstrated.

76	  `fastest`, `composable`, `regressions` (self-join), `roofline` answer

80	- A written account (in the base's `README.md`) of what the opaque column

85	## R3 — LEP-0002, typed predicate IR
86	
87	Landed in three commits: field symbols (`Ticket.Field`, `FieldOf`,
88	`Entity.columns` computed), the IR (`Col` indexed by its storage codec,
89	`Pred` with `opaque` leaves, `denote`, `approx_sound` proved), and the

98	
99	Both written 2026-09-01 from R1/R2 evidence; implementation order below.
100	
101	- **LEP-0004, child-table quantifiers** — landed. `exists`/`forall` in
102	  `Pred` (now an inductive family over `ts`), `Snapshot` denotation,
103	  `approx_sound` extended, alias-function rendering (`describe` byte-
104	  identical), `selectP` taking a plan as data, `pred%`, `Pred.all`/`any`.
105	  eats' `suitable` is one `selectP` rendering nested `NOT EXISTS`, with a

107	  identical everywhere but the two `suitable` lines.
108	- **LEP-0003, nested values.** B1–B3 landed: `deriving LeanDb.DbJson`
109	  (defaults honoured, Lean-compatible encoding), `JsonShape` carried on
110	  the codec into `ColumnSpec`, the fingerprint and `schema_json`;
111	  `planMigration` restamps additive-with-defaults shape changes and
112	  refuses the rest by name; derived columns via `:= derived expr`
113	  (attributes are not allowed on fields) recomputed on write and checked
114	  on read. kernels: `KernelSig`/`LaunchConfig` through `ColCodec.json`,
115	  search columns derived, raw-SQL desync refused on read; every
116	  shape-less base's fingerprint unchanged. **A landed:** `EnumSet α` as an
117	  INTEGER bitmask with a mask CHECK, drift scan, names-array JSON,
118	  `Pred.bit` (membership pushes as `(col & ?) != 0`, `a ∈ s` recognized),
119	  migrations append/truncate only (reorder/middle-removal refused — bits
120	  would change meaning), fingerprint covers the variant names; kernels'
121	  `fuses` uses it. **C landed:** `deriving LeanDb.Inline`; a parent flattens an inline
122	  field into `f_sub` columns with flat symbols, `group` for nested row
123	  JSON (both spellings accepted, both-at-once refused), split defaults,
124	  `colOf?` resolves `k.val.launch.smemBytes` to the flattened symbol;
125	  kernels' `LaunchConfig` and `NumericProps` inline. eats' `KindSet` is
126	  now `EnumSet`. **D landed:** `List R` of an `Inline` record is a

128	  `parent`, `position`), attached on every read, written in the verb's
129	  transaction, nested in row JSON; `.any`/`.all` over the list reify to

136	
137	Modifiers and variants as a stored function over a finite configuration

1	# Changelog
2	
3	## Unreleased
4	
5	Pushdown: comparisons through a validated newtype's projection push when
6	the projection is the column's encoding (checked by definitional
7	equality); case splits on captured closed-enum parameters; value/value
8	guards fold at plan build; `if`/`cond` on columns reify. BLOB columns are
9	a typed `decode` error naming table and field. Constraint classification
10	matches extended result codes first and message text case-insensitively.
11	The importer reports UNIQUE constraints from `PRAGMA index_list`, named
12	by column list, and detects CHECK token- and quote-aware. `rows --eq`
13	splits at the first `=`.
14	
15	Two new bases: `examples/eats` (restaurants; dietary suitability computed
16	from ingredients, never stored) and `examples/kernels` (GPU kernels with
17	typed signatures and composition, benches keyed by gpumarket's `Gpu`).
18	
19	LEP-0002 landed: `deriving LeanDb.Entity` generates field symbols
20	(`Ticket.Field`) and `select` carries an intrinsically typed plan
21	`Pred ts` — column references are Lean values indexed by the storage
22	codec, ordered comparisons require `SqlOrd` at the constructor, the
23	residual is an `opaque` leaf, `denote` gives every plan a meaning, and
24	`approx_sound` proves the pushed fragment never excludes a row the lambda
25	accepts. `PushPred` is gone; every base's logged plan is byte-identical.
26	`rows --eq` decodes its value through the column's codec.
27	
28	LEP-0004 landed: `Pred.exists`/`Pred.forall` over a related table,
29	denoted against a `Snapshot`, rendered as `EXISTS`/`NOT EXISTS`,
30	covered by `approx_sound`; `selectP` takes a plan as data and `pred%`
31	reifies a lambda into one. eats' `suitable` is a single query.
32	
33	LEP-0003 B landed: `deriving LeanDb.DbJson` honours structure defaults;
34	JSON columns carry a type shape that the fingerprint, `schema_json` and
35	the migration diff see (additive-with-defaults changes restamp, others
36	are refused by name); `:= derived expr` columns are recomputed on write
37	and checked on read. kernels' signature and search columns use them.
38	
39	LEP-0003 A landed: `EnumSet α` bitmask columns over a closed world —
40	mask CHECK, open-time drift scan, JSON as an array of names, `Pred.bit`
41	so membership pushes; kernels' `fuses`.
42	
43	LEP-0003 C landed: `deriving LeanDb.Inline` — small fixed structures
44	flatten into prefixed columns with flat field symbols, nested row JSON
45	(both spellings accepted), split defaults, and full pushdown through the
46	projection; kernels' `LaunchConfig`/`NumericProps`.
47	
48	LEP-0003 D landed: a field `ins : List R` with `R` an `Inline` record is
49	a child table — the derive declares the entity `Parent.Ins` (`parent :
50	Ref Parent` with `ON DELETE CASCADE`, `position`, the record's fields),
51	`Entity.children` describes it (`ChildLink`) and `Entity.specs` lists it.
52	The list is part of the value: every read attaches it (one `IN (…)`
53	fetch per child table, chunked), `insert`/`update` write it in a
54	transaction, `delete` cascades. Row JSON nests it as an array of records.
55	`xs.any f`/`xs.all f` over a child-list field reify to LEP-0004's
56	`exists`/`forall`. A derived column may read a child list; its check
57	runs at attach time. `ColumnSpec.cascade`. kernels' `ins`/`outs`.
58	
59	Pushdown: a captured `Option α` parameter over a closed world case-splits
60	(`none` and each `some c`), so "filter by X if given" pushes in both the
61	`isNone ||` and the `match` spelling; `some a == some b` unwraps.
62	
63	LEP-0005 stage 1 (eats): configurable espresso offers — a finite
64	configuration type with a validity predicate, typed option patterns, a
65	price rule with `decide`d lints, a tabulated `offer_price` table, order
66	lines quoted against it; seven configuration queries and a second test
67	executable.
68	Design docs: LEP-0002, the kernels/restaurants stress study, `ROADMAP.md`.
69	
70	## 0.2.0 - 2026-08-25
71	
72	LeanDB 0.2.0 replaces the earlier decision-query prototype with a typed SQLite engine. Entity structures now derive their table schema, codecs, DDL, JSON representation, CLI operations, migration plan, and schema fingerprint from one Lean definition.
73	
74	The release includes typed row IDs and foreign references, compare-and-swap updates, restricted deletes, closed enums, multi-table selects, safe SQL pushdown, deterministic sorting, schema migrations, query logging, JSON-lines serving, and the `query%` CLI adapter. `leandb import-sqlite` can generate an editable Lean package and an explicit report of source features it could not carry.
75	
76	Seven standalone bases exercise the engine: tickets, CRM, shop, GPUs, GPU Market, Price Watch, and a generated legacy SQLite import.
77	
78	Release review also tightened several boundaries:
79	
80	- UInt16 and UInt32 decoding now rejects the first out-of-range value instead of wrapping to zero.
81	- Inserts and partial updates reject non-object JSON and unknown fields.
82	- CLI row IDs and integer filters reject values outside SQLite's Int64 range.
83	- SQL identifiers and enum literals are escaped correctly.
84	- Zero-field entities use valid SQLite insert and update statements.
85	- Invalid schemas and corrupt migration metadata fail before the database is changed.
86	- Ordered predicate pushdown is limited to codecs that preserve Lean ordering in SQLite.
87	- The SQLite importer refuses to overwrite generated files and reports source defaults and foreign-key actions that a later table rebuild would not preserve.
88

=== leandb-lean-pitfalls.md
---
name: leandb-lean-pitfalls
description: Lean 4.31 / leansqlite gotchas that repeatedly bit us in LeanDB work
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: f988ea15-c535-4c9f-854a-0202fc152073
  modified: 2026-08-24T09:25:21.870Z
---

Recurring Lean v4.31.0 pitfalls in the LeanDB codebase (each cost a build cycle at least once; agent briefings should include them):
- `x |>.foo == y` parses as `x |> (.foo == y)` — parenthesize `((x).foo == y)`.
- `String.take` returns `String.Slice` (call `.toString`); `String.trim` is deprecated → `s.trimAscii.toString`.
- Don't name structures `Task` or `Order` (core clashes). Field `at` needs `«at»` everywhere.
- Doc comments `/-- -/` cannot precede `#check_failure`; use `--` comments. `#check_failure` exists and is the right negative-test tool.
- Deriving on phantom-param structs (like `Id α`) constrains the phantom (`Ord α`) — write manual instances instead.
- leansqlite lowercases the first letter of error messages ("cHECK constraint failed"); match on `IO.Error.otherError 19 details`, not message prefixes. Extended errcodes are NOT enabled — FK vs UNIQUE vs CHECK all arrive as primary code 19, distinguished by message text.
- In elaborators: `whnfCore` won't delta-reduce projection fns (`Prod.fst (Prod.mk a b)` stays put) — use `whnfR` for reducible unfolding; matchers reduce under whnf when the scrutinee is a constructor.
- Names quoted inside syntax quotations resolve at quotation site; a wrong namespace becomes a hygienic `✝` unknown-identifier error at the USE site (confusing) — double-check full names in `` `(...) ``.
- zsh: `echo ===` fails (`=cmd` expansion); Bash tool cwd persists across calls — use absolute paths after any `cd`.
- LCNF ExplicitBoxing PANIC ("unknown join point") on v4.31 for closed top-level terms that (a) contain a String-motive `casesOn` or (b) reference a structure-default `_default` constant. Workarounds shipped: ClosedEnum derives via a scalar-Nat-motive casesOn indexing a variants array; defaults are *evaluated* at derive time (evalExpr on the default fn's `.value!`, definition-site instances baked in) and embedded as Col literals.
- Two sequential `match` statements in one do-block can mis-parse (arms absorbed) — linearize with `.toOption.bind`/helpers instead.
- Don't delab-then-re-elaborate elaborated terms across contexts: instance synthesis re-runs at the new site and can resolve scoped instances differently (silent wrong values). Evaluate or splice the original Expr instead.

**Why:** these are toolchain-version-specific and not documented together anywhere; rediscovering each costs build iterations.
**How to apply:** paste the relevant subset into any subagent prompt that writes Lean for this repo; check this list first when a weird parse/elab error appears.

LeanDB (strongly typed SQL in Lean 4, ~/code/leandb_v2) was rebuilt from scratch starting 2026-08-23 after the v0.1 slice was discarded (review in plan-v2.md appendix; v0.1 preserved at commit 94f04f7). Governing docs: plan.md (interface spec), plan-v2.md (milestones, all ✅ through M6 as of 2026-08-24).

Key architecture decisions (argued in plan-v2, don't relitigate):
- Engine (`LeanDb` lib) imports no domain; bases are separate Lake packages under examples/ requiring leandb by path. Four bases: tickets, crm, shop, gpus — each with tests + CLI_TRANSCRIPT.md.
- `select` keeps plain-lambda semantics; pushdown is a fetch-narrowing prefilter reified by the `leandb_plan` tactic into a `PushPred` tree via a `PlanFor where' := by leandb_plan` autoParam. The lambda is ALWAYS applied client-side, so plans can only optimize, never change results (differential tests pin this).
- match on closed enums compiles to SQL by case-splitting on the world (⋁ col IS 'c' ∧ branch); `@[db]`-tagged defs unfold during reification.
- Migrations v1: instance stores schema as JSON in _leandb_meta; diff → additive auto-apply, shape changes rebuild the table, drops need --allow-destructive.
- SQLite via leanprover/leansqlite pinned at rev 0be4df908d1a8e75b58961041e2b4973692623df (last commit on lean4 v4.31.0 — bump in lockstep with lean-toolchain).

Still deferred by name: SQL import (agent work, near done), MCP/HTTP serve (JSONL `serve` exists), log replay, --output-lean, migration source-file synthesis. See [[leandb-lean-pitfalls]].

=== leandb-thesis-one-universe.md
---
name: leandb-thesis-one-universe
description: The user's stated thesis for LeanDB — queries, data and migrations in one typed universe so a vocabulary edit shows its impact on usage, not just data
metadata:
  type: project
---

The user's core thesis (stated 2026-09-01): the advantage of typed queries + typed data + typed migrations being one universe is that an edit to the vocabulary shows its *impact on usage*, not only on stored data — e.g. adding a modifier variant, the compiler says where pricing must be reconsidered. Recorded in `proposals/LEP-0005-configurable-entities.md`, section "Vocabulary growth: what the compiler sees, what the migration sees": compiler for facts-as-code (non-exhaustive match), migration-time rule-coverage check for facts-as-rows (finite typed config space), query replay for plans (R5).

**Why:** this is the criterion the user judges designs by ("pretty unique"); proposals should say explicitly which of the three reports a feature enables.

**How to apply:** when designing an engine feature or a base, state what a vocabulary edit does at build time, at `migrate status`, and to existing queries. Related: [[leandb-roadmap-state]].
=== leandb-verification-baseline.md
---
name: leandb-verification-baseline
description: How pushdown changes in LeanDB are verified — replay transcripts, diff logged plans byte-for-byte
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Any change to LeanDB's plan tactic or executor is verified by replaying every base's `CLI_TRANSCRIPT.md` commands against a fresh instance and diffing the logged `select` plans (`<base> log` detail strings) against a pre-change baseline — zero differences is the bar — in addition to `scripts/release_check.sh`. A replay script (`plans_baseline.py`, ~30 lines: parse `$ <base> …` lines from the transcript, run them, dump `log`) was written in the session scratchpad and is not in the repo; recreate it if needed.

**Why:** LEP-0002 was accepted on "every base's logged plan byte-identical before and after"; the user cares that pushdown is observationally invisible.

**How to apply:** capture the baseline BEFORE touching PlanElab/Pred/Db; compare after; treat any diff as a bug unless the old plan was provably wrong. Related: [[leandb-roadmap-state]].

1	import LeanDb.Db
2	import LeanDb.Json
3	import LeanDb.Migrate
4	
5	namespace LeanDb.Cli
6	
7	/-! # The derived CLI
8	
9	A base gets a machine-first CLI by listing its entities and queries; every
10	verb's behavior and JSON shape is derived from `Entity` instances. Exit
11	codes per plan.md §4.5: 0 ok, 2 typed `DbError` (JSON on stderr), 3 usage,
12	4 schema/version mismatch (`DbError.exitCode`).
13	The argv boundary is the one place strings are inherent; they are parsed
14	into types immediately and everything past this module is typed.
15	-/
16	
17	open Lean (Json)
18	
19	/-- How a CLI/serve argument string parses into a typed value. Closed
20	    enums parse by variant name for free; bases add instances for their
21	    newtypes. -/
22	class CliArg (α : Type) where
23	  parse : String → Except String α
24	
25	instance : CliArg Nat := ⟨fun s => match s.toNat? with
26	  | some n => .ok n
27	  | none => .error s!"expected a natural number, got {String.quote s}"⟩
28	
29	instance : CliArg Int64 := ⟨fun s => match s.toInt? with
30	  | some i =>
31	      if i < Int64.minValue.toInt || i > Int64.maxValue.toInt then
32	        .error s!"integer out of Int64 range: {s}"
33	      else .ok (Int64.ofInt i)
34	  | none => .error s!"expected an integer, got {String.quote s}"⟩
35	
36	instance : CliArg String := ⟨.ok⟩
37	
38	instance : CliArg (Id α) := ⟨fun s => do
39	  let n ← (CliArg.parse s : Except String Nat)
40	  if n > Int64.maxValue.toNatClampNeg then
41	    throw s!"row id out of Int64 range: {s}"
42	  return ⟨Int64.ofNat n⟩⟩
43	
44	instance [ClosedEnum α] : CliArg α := ⟨fun s =>
45	  match ClosedEnum.decodeName s with
46	  | some a => .ok a
47	  | none => .error s!"{String.quote s} is not one of {ClosedEnum.variants α}"⟩
48	
49	/-- How a query result renders as JSON. -/
50	class QueryOut (α : Type) where
51	  json : α → Json
52	
53	instance [Entity α] : QueryOut (Stored α) := ⟨rowJson α⟩
54	instance [QueryOut α] [QueryOut β] : QueryOut (α × β) :=
55	  ⟨fun (a, b) => Json.arr #[QueryOut.json a, QueryOut.json b]⟩
56	instance [QueryOut α] : QueryOut (Array α) := ⟨fun xs => Json.arr (xs.map QueryOut.json)⟩
57	instance [QueryOut α] : QueryOut (List α) := ⟨fun xs => Json.arr (xs.map QueryOut.json).toArray⟩
58	instance [QueryOut α] : QueryOut (Option α) :=
59	  ⟨fun | none => Json.null | some a => QueryOut.json a⟩
60	instance : QueryOut Nat := ⟨Lean.toJson⟩
61	instance : QueryOut String := ⟨Json.str⟩
62	instance : QueryOut Bool := ⟨Json.bool⟩
63	instance : QueryOut Unit := ⟨fun _ => Json.null⟩
64	instance : QueryOut Json := ⟨id⟩
65	
66	/-- Pop one typed positional argument (used by `query%`-derived handlers). -/
67	def popArg (α : Type) [CliArg α] (name : String) (args : List String) :
68	    DbM (α × List String) := do
69	  match args with
70	  | [] => throw (.decode "cli" name "missing argument")
71	  | a :: rest =>
72	      match CliArg.parse (α := α) a with
73	      | .ok v => return (v, rest)
74	      | .error m => throw (.decode "cli" name m)
75	
76	def doneArgs : List String → DbM Unit
77	  | [] => pure ()
78	  | extra => throw (.decode "cli" "args" s!"unexpected extra arguments {extra}")
79	
80	def okResult (j : Json) : Json := Json.mkObj [("ok", Json.bool true), ("result", j)]
81	
82	structure CliTable where
83	  name : String
84	  insertJson : Json → DbM Json
85	  getJson : Int64 → DbM Json
86	  updateJson : Int64 → Json → DbM Json
87	  deleteRow : Int64 → DbM Json
88	  /-- `rows` with conjunctive equality filters (plan.md §4.1: `--eq` and
89	      limit are the CLI's whole filter language — anything more is a
90	      typed query). -/
91	  rowsWhere : List (String × String) → Nat → DbM Json
92	
93	private def okRow (j : Json) : Json := Json.mkObj [("ok", Json.bool true), ("row", j)]
94	
95	def CliTable.of (α : Type) [Entity α] : CliTable where
96	  name := Entity.tableName α
97	  insertJson j := do
98	    let a ← DbM.ofExcept (rowOfJson α j)
99	    return okRow (rowJson α (← insert α a))
100	  getJson id := do
101	    match ← get (⟨id⟩ : Id α) with
102	    | some s => return okRow (rowJson α s)
103	    | none => throw (.notFound (Entity.tableName α) id)
104	  updateJson id j := do
105	    match ← get (⟨id⟩ : Id α) with
106	    | some old =>
107	        let new ← DbM.ofExcept (rowMergeJson α old.val j)
108	        return okRow (rowJson α (← update old new))
109	    | none => throw (.notFound (Entity.tableName α) id)
110	  deleteRow id := do
111	    delete (⟨id⟩ : Id α)
112	    return Json.mkObj [("ok", Json.bool true), ("deleted", Lean.toJson id.toInt)]
113	  rowsWhere eqs limit := do
114	    let spec := Entity.spec α
115	    -- (symbol, typed value) per filter; the plan is folded from these
116	    -- below, outside the monad (`Pred` lives in `Type 1`, `DbM` carries `Type`)
117	    let mut conds : Array ((f : Entity.Field α) × Entity.fieldTy f) := #[]
118	    for (col, v) in eqs do
119	      -- the boundary parses the name into the symbol at once; from here
120	      -- on the column is `f`, never the string
121	      match Entity.fieldOfName? α col with
122	      | none =>
123	          throw (.decode spec.name col
124	            s!"no such column; columns: {spec.columns.toList.map (·.name)}")
125	      | some f =>
126	          let c := Entity.fieldSpec f
127	          -- a closed-world column refuses unknown variants loudly — a
128	          -- silent empty result is the exact failure mode LeanDB exists
129	          -- to kill
130	          if let some vs := c.enum then
131	            unless vs.contains v do
132	              throw (.decode spec.name col
133	                s!"{String.quote v} is not in the closed world {vs}")
134	          let cv ← match c.sqlType with
135	            | .integer =>
136	                match v.toInt? with
137	                | some i =>
138	                    if i < Int64.minValue.toInt || i > Int64.maxValue.toInt then
139	                      throw (.decode spec.name col s!"integer out of Int64 range: {v}")
140	                    pure (Col.int (Int64.ofInt i))
141	                | none => throw (.decode spec.name col s!"expected an integer, got {String.quote v}")
142	            | .text => pure (Col.text v)
143	            | .real => throw (.decode spec.name col "REAL columns cannot be filtered with --eq")
144	          -- the validated value goes through the column's own codec, like
145	          -- every other boundary: a validated newtype's canonical encoding
146	          -- is what SQLite compares, not the spelling on the command line
147	          let tv ← match (Entity.codec f).fromCol cv with
148	            | .ok tv => pure tv
149	            | .error e => throw (.decode spec.name col e)
150	          conds := conds.push ⟨f, tv⟩
151	    let pred : Pred [α] := conds.foldl (init := .tt) fun p c => p.andS (.eq (.here c.1) .eq c.2)
152	    let rows ← fetchFiltered α pred
153	    let rows := rows.toList.take limit
154	    return Json.mkObj [("ok", Json.bool true), ("count", Lean.toJson rows.length),
155	      ("rows", Json.arr (rows.map (rowJson α)).toArray)]
156	
157	/-- A base, as the CLI sees it: name, default instance path, specs (both
158	    derived from the types), tables, and named queries. An entity with
159	    child lists (LEP-0003 D) contributes `Entity.specs α` — its table and
160	    its child tables — and lists the children as tables of their own
161	    (`.of Kernel.Ins`) so `rows kernel_ins --eq …` works like any other
162	    table; `rows kernel` shows the lists nested. -/
163	structure Base where
164	  name : String
165	  dbPath : System.FilePath
166	  specs : List TableSpec
167	  tables : List CliTable
168	  queries : List (String × (List String → DbM Json)) := []
169	
170	private def usageJson (b : Base) : Json :=
171	  Json.mkObj [
172	    ("ok", Json.bool true),
173	    ("base", Json.str b.name),
174	    ("usage", Json.arr #[
175	      Json.str "schema",
176	      Json.str "insert <table> <json>",
177	      Json.str "get <table> <id>",
178	      Json.str "update <table> <id> <partial-json>",
179	      Json.str "delete <table> <id>",
180	      Json.str "rows <table> [--eq col=value]... [--limit n]",
181	      Json.str "version",
182	      Json.str "query <name> [args...]",
183	      Json.str "log [limit]",
184	      Json.str "migrate status | apply [--allow-destructive]",
185	      Json.str "serve  (JSON-lines over stdio, persistent connection)"]),
186	    ("tables", Json.arr (b.tables.map (Json.str ·.name)).toArray),
187	    ("queries", Json.arr (b.queries.map (Json.str ·.1)).toArray)]
188	
189	private def parseId (s : String) : Except String Int64 :=
190	  match s.toNat? with
191	  | some n =>
192	      if n > Int64.maxValue.toNatClampNeg then
193	        .error s!"row id out of Int64 range: {s}"
194	      else .ok (Int64.ofNat n)
195	  | none => .error s!"expected a row id, got {String.quote s}"
196	
197	private def parseJson (s : String) : Except String Json := Json.parse s
198	
199	private def table? (b : Base) (name : String) : Except String CliTable :=
200	  match b.tables.find? (·.name == name) with
201	  | some t => .ok t
202	  | none => .error s!"unknown table {String.quote name}; tables: {b.tables.map (·.name)}"
203	
204	private def logJson (limit : Nat) : DbM Json := do
205	  let rows ← readLog limit
206	  return Json.mkObj [("ok", Json.bool true), ("count", Lean.toJson rows.size),
207	    ("entries", Json.arr rows)]
208	
209	/-- `rows` flags: `--eq col=value`… `--limit n` (or a bare trailing limit). -/
210	private def parseRowFlags : List String → List (String × String) → Nat →
211	    Except String (List (String × String) × Nat)
212	  | [], eqs, limit => .ok (eqs.reverse, limit)
213	  | "--eq" :: kv :: rest, eqs, limit =>
214	      -- split at the first `=` only: a value may itself contain `=`
215	      -- (a canonical `M=4096,N=4096` binding, say)
216	      match kv.splitOn "=" with
217	      | k :: v :: vs => parseRowFlags rest ((k, String.intercalate "=" (v :: vs)) :: eqs) limit
218	      | _ => .error s!"--eq expects col=value, got {String.quote kv}"
219	  | "--limit" :: n :: rest, eqs, _ =>
220	      match n.toNat? with
221	      | some limit => parseRowFlags rest eqs limit
222	      | none => .error s!"--limit expects a number, got {String.quote n}"
223	  | [n], eqs, _ =>
224	      match n.toNat? with
225	      | some limit => .ok (eqs.reverse, limit)
226	      | none => .error s!"unrecognized rows argument {String.quote n}"
227	  | arg :: _, _, _ => .error s!"unrecognized rows argument {String.quote arg}"
228	
229	/-- Resolve argv into one typed database action (or a usage error). -/
230	private def command (b : Base) : List String → Except String (DbM Json)
231	  | ["insert", t, j] => do pure ((← table? b t).insertJson (← parseJson j))
232	  | ["get", t, i] => do pure ((← table? b t).getJson (← parseId i))
233	  | ["update", t, i, j] => do
234	      pure ((← table? b t).updateJson (← parseId i) (← parseJson j))
235	  | ["delete", t, i] => do pure ((← table? b t).deleteRow (← parseId i))
236	  | ["log"] => .ok (logJson 50)
237	  | ["log", n] => do
238	      let some limit := n.toNat? | throw s!"expected a limit, got {String.quote n}"
239	      pure (logJson limit)
240	  | "rows" :: t :: flags => do
241	      let tbl ← table? b t
242	      let (eqs, limit) ← parseRowFlags flags [] 100
243	      pure (tbl.rowsWhere eqs limit)
244	  | "query" :: name :: qargs =>
245	      match b.queries.find? (·.1 == name) with
246	      | some (_, q) => .ok (q qargs)
247	      | none => .error s!"unknown query {String.quote name}; queries: {b.queries.map (·.1)}"
248	  | args => .error s!"unrecognized command {args}"
249	
250	/-- Served mode: JSON-lines over stdio against one persistent connection.
251	    Each request line is a JSON array of argv strings; each response is one
252	    JSON object line. EOF ends the session. -/
253	def serve (b : Base) : IO UInt32 := do
254	  if let some parent := b.dbPath.parent then
255	    IO.FS.createDirAll parent
256	  match ← openDb b.dbPath b.specs with
257	  | .error e =>
258	      IO.eprintln e.toJson.compress
259	      return e.exitCode
260	  | .ok conn =>
261	      let stdin ← IO.getStdin
262	      let out ← IO.getStdout
263	      repeat
264	        let line ← stdin.getLine
265	        if line.isEmpty then break
266	        let line := line.trimAscii.toString
267	        if line.isEmpty then continue
268	        let argv? := Lean.Json.parse line >>= fun j => do
269	          let arr ← j.getArr?
270	          arr.toList.mapM (·.getStr?)
271	        match argv? with
272	        | .error m =>
273	            out.putStrLn (Json.mkObj [("ok", Json.bool false), ("code", Json.str "usage"),
274	              ("message", Json.str s!"expected a JSON array of argv strings: {m}")]).compress
275	        | .ok ["schema"] =>
276	            out.putStrLn (schemaJson b.name b.specs).compress
277	        | .ok argv =>
278	            match command b argv with
279	            | .error m =>
280	                out.putStrLn (Json.mkObj [("ok", Json.bool false),
281	                  ("code", Json.str "usage"), ("message", Json.str m)]).compress
282	            | .ok act =>
283	                match ← act.run conn with
284	                | .ok j => out.putStrLn j.compress
285	                | .error e => out.putStrLn e.toJson.compress
286	        out.flush
287	      return 0
288	
289	def run (b : Base) (args : List String) : IO UInt32 := do
290	  match args with
291	  | ["serve"] => serve b
292	  | [] | ["help"] | ["--help"] =>
293	      IO.println (usageJson b).compress
294	      return 0
295	  | ["schema"] =>
296	      IO.println (schemaJson b.name b.specs).compress
297	      return 0
298	  | ["version"] =>
299	      let codeFp := fingerprint b.specs
300	      let (instFp, instVer) ← do
301	        match ← instanceInfo b.dbPath with
302	        | none => pure (Json.null, Json.null)
303	        | some (fp, ver) =>
304	            pure (fp.map Json.str |>.getD Json.null,
305	              (ver.map fun v => Lean.toJson v).getD Json.null)
306	      IO.println (Json.mkObj [("ok", Json.bool true),
307	        ("code_fingerprint", Json.str codeFp),
308	        ("instance_fingerprint", instFp),
309	        ("schema_version", instVer),
310	        ("in_sync", Json.bool (instFp == Json.str codeFp))]).compress
311	      return 0
312	  | "migrate" :: rest =>
313	      let apply ← match rest with
314	        | ["status"] => pure (some (false, false))
315	        | ["apply"] => pure (some (true, false))
316	        | ["apply", "--allow-destructive"] => pure (some (true, true))
317	        | _ => pure none
318	      match apply with
319	      | none =>
320	          IO.eprintln (Json.mkObj [("ok", Json.bool false), ("code", Json.str "usage"),
321	            ("message", Json.str "migrate status | apply [--allow-destructive]")]).compress
322	          return 3
323	      | some (apply, allowDestructive) =>
324	          if let some parent := b.dbPath.parent then
325	            IO.FS.createDirAll parent
326	          match ← migrate b.dbPath b.specs apply allowDestructive with
327	          | .error e =>
328	              IO.eprintln e.toJson.compress
329	              return 2
330	          | .ok (plan?, report?) =>
331	              match report? with
332	              | some r => IO.println r.toJson.compress
333	              | none =>
334	                  let plan := plan?.getD {}
335	                  IO.println (Json.mkObj [("ok", Json.bool true),
336	                    ("steps", Json.arr (plan.steps.map (Json.str ·.describe)).toArray),
337	                    ("destructive", Json.bool plan.isDestructive),
338	                    ("notes", Json.arr (plan.notes.map Json.str).toArray)]).compress
339	              return 0
340	  | args =>
341	      match command b args with
342	      | .error msg =>
343	          IO.eprintln (Json.mkObj [("ok", Json.bool false), ("code", Json.str "usage"),
344	            ("message", Json.str msg)]).compress
345	          return 3
346	      | .ok act =>
347	          if let some parent := b.dbPath.parent then
348	            IO.FS.createDirAll parent
349	          match ← withDb b.dbPath b.specs act with
350	          | .ok j =>
351	              IO.println j.compress
352	              return 0
353	          | .error e =>
354	              IO.eprintln e.toJson.compress
355	              return e.exitCode
356	
357	end LeanDb.Cli

1	import LeanDb.Db
2	import LeanDb.Json
3	
4	namespace LeanDb
5	
6	/-! # Migrations v1: additive auto-migration, loud destruction
7	
8	The instance remembers the schema it was last shaped to (`schema_json` in
9	`_leandb_meta`). `planMigration` diffs that against the code's specs and
10	produces steps:
11	
12	- new table → `CREATE TABLE`;
13	- new column → `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` — the column must be nullable
14	  (`Option`), because existing rows need a value and v1 refuses to invent
15	  one (backfills are a judgment call, per plan.md §6);
16	- changed column (type, nullability, FK target, or a changed closed world)
17	  → table rebuild: create under a scratch name with the new DDL, copy the
18	  surviving columns, drop, rename. A *shrunk* closed world hits the new
19	  CHECK during the copy and aborts the transaction — vocabulary can only
20	  shrink through a migration, and only when the data already conforms;
21	- dropped column/table → destructive, refused unless explicitly allowed;
22	- a JSON column whose declared *shape* changed (LEP-0003 B2): additive
23	  with defaults (fields added, each with a default; constructors or
24	  variants added) → `restampShape`, a step with no SQL that exists so
25	  the change is journaled; anything else (a field removed or retyped, a
26	  constructor renamed or removed, a nested closed world shrunk) is
27	  refused by name — a typed value transformation is not yet available.
28	
29	Everything applies in one transaction with a foreign-key check before
30	commit. `openDb` still refuses fingerprint drift; `migrate` is the one
31	explicit gate through which schemas move.
32	-/
33	
34	inductive MigStep where
35	  | createTable (spec : TableSpec)
36	  | addColumn (table : String) (col : ColumnSpec)
37	  | dropColumn (table col : String)
38	  | dropTable (name : String)
39	  /-- Rebuild `spec.name` under the new spec, copying `copyCols`. -/
40	  | rebuildTable (spec : TableSpec) (copyCols : List String)
41	  /-- A JSON column's declared shape changed additively: no SQL, every
42	      stored value still decodes; the step exists to be journaled. -/
43	  | restampShape (table col : String)
44	  deriving Repr
45	
46	def MigStep.describe : MigStep → String
47	  | .createTable spec => s!"create table \"{spec.name}\""
48	  | .addColumn t c => s!"add column \"{t}\".\"{c.name}\""
49	  | .dropColumn t c => s!"DROP column \"{t}\".\"{c}\""
50	  | .dropTable t => s!"DROP table \"{t}\""
51	  | .rebuildTable spec cols =>
52	      s!"rebuild table \"{spec.name}\" (copying {cols.length} columns)"
53	  | .restampShape t c => s!"restamp shape of \"{t}\".\"{c}\""
54	
55	def MigStep.destructive : MigStep → Bool
56	  | .dropColumn .. | .dropTable .. => true
57	  | _ => false
58	
59	def MigStep.sql : MigStep → List String
60	  | .createTable spec => [spec.ddl]
61	  | .addColumn t c => [s!"ALTER TABLE {quoteIdent t} ADD COLUMN {c.ddlFragment}"]
62	  | .dropColumn t c => [s!"ALTER TABLE {quoteIdent t} DROP COLUMN {quoteIdent c}"]
63	  | .dropTable t => [s!"DROP TABLE {quoteIdent t}"]
64	  | .rebuildTable spec copyCols =>
65	      let tmp := s!"_leandb_new_{spec.name}"
66	      let cols := String.intercalate ", " ("id" :: copyCols.map quoteIdent)
67	      [ spec.ddlNamed tmp (ifNotExists := false),
68	        s!"INSERT INTO {quoteIdent tmp} ({cols}) SELECT {cols} FROM {quoteIdent spec.name}",
69	        s!"DROP TABLE {quoteIdent spec.name}",
70	        s!"ALTER TABLE {quoteIdent tmp} RENAME TO {quoteIdent spec.name}" ]
71	  | .restampShape .. => []
72	
73	/-! ## Shapes
74	
75	`JsonShape.shape` strings (grammar documented on the class) parsed back
76	into a tree, so two schemas' shapes can be *compared*, not just found
77	unequal. -/
78	
79	/-- A parsed shape. An inductive constructor's payload is `(named, fields)`:
80	    a named record (object encoding), or positional (`named = false`, the
81	    field names empty; array encoding), or nothing (`fields = []`). -/
82	inductive Shape where
83	  | prim (name : String)
84	  | struct (name : String) (fields : List (String × Shape × Bool))
85	  | ind (name : String) (ctors : List (String × Bool × List (String × Shape)))
86	  | closed (variants : List String)
87	  | list (of : Shape)
88	  | option (of : Shape)
89	  | pair (a b : Shape)
90	  deriving Repr, Inhabited
91	
92	/-- Back to the canonical string (diagnostics). -/
93	partial def Shape.render : Shape → String
94	  | .prim n => n
95	  | .struct n fs => JsonShape.struct n (fs.map fun (f, s, d) => (f, s.render, d))
96	  | .ind n cs => JsonShape.inductive' n (cs.map fun (c, named, fs) =>
97	      (c, if fs.isEmpty then .none
98	          else if named then .named (fs.map fun (f, s) => (f, s.render))
99	          else .positional (fs.map fun (_, s) => s.render)))
100	  | .closed vs => JsonShape.closed vs.toArray
101	  | .list s => JsonShape.list s.render
102	  | .option s => JsonShape.option s.render
103	  | .pair a b => JsonShape.pair a.render b.render
104	
105	namespace Shape
106	
107	private def isDelim (c : Char) : Bool :=
108	  c == '{' || c == '}' || c == '(' || c == ')' || c == '<' || c == '>' ||
109	  c == '[' || c == ']' || c == ',' || c == '|' || c == ':' || c == '?' || c == '='
110	
111	private def takeName (cs : List Char) : Except String (String × List Char) :=
112	  let name := cs.takeWhile (!isDelim ·)
113	  if name.isEmpty then .error s!"expected a name at {String.ofList (cs.take 12)}"
114	  else .ok (String.ofList name, cs.drop name.length)
115	
116	private def expect (c : Char) (cs : List Char) : Except String (List Char) :=
117	  match cs with
118	  | d :: rest => if d == c then .ok rest else .error s!"expected '{c}', found '{d}'"
119	  | [] => .error s!"expected '{c}', found end of shape"
120	
121	private def suffix (s : Shape) : List Char → Shape × List Char
122	  | '?' :: r => suffix (.option s) r
123	  | r => (s, r)
124	
125	private partial def variants (acc : List String) (r : List Char) :
126	    Except String (List String × List Char) := do
127	  let (v, r) ← takeName r
128	  match r with
129	  | '|' :: r => variants (acc ++ [v]) r
130	  | '>' :: r => return (acc ++ [v], r)
131	  | _ => throw "expected '|' or '>' in a closed world"
132	
133	mutual
134	  private partial def parseShape (cs : List Char) : Except String (Shape × List Char) := do
135	    let (base, rest) ← parseAtom cs
136	    return suffix base rest
137	
138	  private partial def parseAtom (cs : List Char) : Except String (Shape × List Char) := do
139	    match cs with
140	    | '[' :: r =>
141	        let (s, r) ← parseShape r
142	        return (.list s, ← expect ']' r)
143	    | '(' :: r =>
144	        let (a, r) ← parseShape r
145	        let r ← expect ',' r
146	        let (b, r) ← parseShape r
147	        return (.pair a b, ← expect ')' r)
148	    | '<' :: r =>
149	        let (vs, r) ← variants [] r
150	        return (.closed vs, r)
151	    | _ =>
152	        let (name, r) ← takeName cs
153	        match r with
154	        | '{' :: '}' :: r => return (.struct name [], r)
155	        | '{' :: r =>
156	            let (fs, r) ← parseFields '}' [] r
157	            return (.struct name fs, r)
158	        | '(' :: r =>
159	            let (cs, r) ← parseCtors [] r
160	            return (.ind name cs, r)
161	        | _ => return (.prim name, r)
162	
163	  /-- `f:S=,g:S` up to `close`; the `Bool` is the `=` marker. -/
164	  private partial def parseFields (close : Char) (acc : List (String × Shape × Bool)) (cs : List Char) :
165	      Except String (List (String × Shape × Bool) × List Char) := do
166	    let (f, r) ← takeName cs
167	    let r ← expect ':' r
168	    let (s, r) ← parseShape r
169	    let (d, r) := match r with | '=' :: r => (true, r) | r => (false, r)
170	    let acc := acc ++ [(f, s, d)]
171	    match r with
172	    | ',' :: r => parseFields close acc r
173	    | c :: r => if c == close then return (acc, r) else throw s!"expected ',' or '{close}', found '{c}'"
174	    | [] => throw "unterminated field list"
175	
176	  private partial def parsePositional (acc : List (String × Shape)) (r : List Char) :
177	      Except String (List (String × Shape) × List Char) := do
178	    let (s, r) ← parseShape r
179	    let acc := acc ++ [("", s)]
180	    match r with
181	    | ',' :: r => parsePositional acc r
182	    | ']' :: r => return (acc, r)
183	    | _ => throw "expected ',' or ']' in a positional payload"
184	
185	  private partial def parseCtors (acc : List (String × Bool × List (String × Shape))) (cs : List Char) :
186	      Except String (List (String × Bool × List (String × Shape)) × List Char) := do
187	    let (c, r) ← takeName cs
188	    let (entry, r) ← match r with
189	      | '{' :: r => do
190	          let (fs, r) ← parseFields '}' [] r
191	          pure ((c, true, fs.map fun (f, s, _) => (f, s)), r)
192	      | '[' :: r => do
193	          let (fs, r) ← parsePositional [] r
194	          pure ((c, false, fs), r)
195	      | r => pure ((c, true, []), r)
196	    let acc := acc ++ [entry]
197	    match r with
198	    | '|' :: r => parseCtors acc r
199	    | ')' :: r => return (acc, r)
200	    | _ => throw "expected '|' or ')' after a constructor"
201	end
202	
203	/-- Parse a `JsonShape` string. -/
204	def parse (s : String) : Except String Shape := do
205	  let (shape, rest) ← parseShape s.toList
206	  unless rest.isEmpty do throw s!"trailing input in shape: {String.ofList rest}"
207	  return shape
208	
209	/-- Is `new` an *additive-with-defaults* change from `old` — every value
210	    encoded under `old` still decodes under `new`? `.ok` if so; otherwise
211	    the first change that breaks it, named. Type names of structures and
212	    inductives are informational (a rename changes no data); everything
213	    that changes an encoding is a refusal. -/
214	partial def additive (old new : Shape) : Except String Unit := do
215	  match old, new with
216	  | .prim a, .prim b =>
217	      unless a == b do throw s!"type changed from `{a}` to `{b}`"
218	  | .struct on ofs, .struct nn nfs =>
219	      for (f, os, _) in ofs do
220	        match nfs.find? (·.1 == f) with
221	        | none => throw s!"field `{f}` removed from `{on}`"
222	        | some (_, ns, _) => additive os ns |>.mapError fun m => s!"field `{f}` of `{on}`: {m}"
223	      for (f, _, d) in nfs do
224	        if (ofs.find? (·.1 == f)).isNone && !d then
225	          throw s!"field `{f}` added to `{nn}` without a default"
226	  | .ind on ocs, .ind _ ncs =>
227	      for (c, onamed, ofs) in ocs do
228	        match ncs.find? (·.1 == c) with
229	        | none => throw s!"constructor `{c}` renamed/removed from `{on}`"
230	        | some (_, nnamed, nfs) =>
231	            unless onamed == nnamed && ofs.length == nfs.length do
232	              throw s!"payload of constructor `{c}` of `{on}` changed"
233	            for ((of', os), (nf, ns)) in ofs.zip nfs do
234	              unless of' == nf do
235	                throw s!"payload field `{of'}` of constructor `{c}` of `{on}` renamed to `{nf}`"
236	              additive os ns |>.mapError fun m => s!"constructor `{c}` of `{on}`: {m}"
237	  | .closed ovs, .closed nvs =>
238	      for v in ovs do
239	        unless nvs.contains v do
240	          throw s!"variant `{v}` removed from the closed world {new.render}"
241	  | .list a, .list b => additive a b |>.mapError fun m => s!"list element: {m}"
242	  | .option a, .option b => additive a b
243	  | a, .option b => additive a b   -- a value of `a` is a value of `a?`
244	  | .pair a b, .pair c d =>
245	      additive a c |>.mapError fun m => s!"first of pair: {m}"
246	      additive b d |>.mapError fun m => s!"second of pair: {m}"
247	  | a, b => throw s!"type changed from `{a.render}` to `{b.render}`"
248	
249	end Shape
250	
251	/-- Classify one column's shape change: `.ok ()` means restamp. -/
252	private def shapeChange (table col : String) (old new : Option String) : Except String Unit := do
253	  match old, new with
254	  | some o, some n =>
255	      let os ← Shape.parse o |>.mapError fun m =>
256	        s!"table \"{table}\": stored shape of column \"{col}\" is unreadable: {m}"
257	      let ns ← Shape.parse n |>.mapError fun m =>
258	        s!"table \"{table}\": declared shape of column \"{col}\" is unreadable: {m}"
259	      Shape.additive os ns |>.mapError fun m =>
260	        s!"table \"{table}\": column \"{col}\" changed shape — {m}. Existing values \
261	would not decode under the new type; a typed value transformation is not yet available, \
262	so this migration is refused. Migrate by hand."
263	  | _, _ => pure ()   -- a shape declared (or dropped) where there was none: nothing to compare
264	
265	structure MigPlan where
266	  steps : List MigStep := []
267	  notes : List String := []
268	  /-- Set by `migrate` from `destructiveAgainst` — step kinds alone miss
269	      rebuilds that drop columns. -/
270	  isDestructive : Bool := false
271	  deriving Repr
272	
273	/-- Diff two schemas into a plan. Errors are refusals with reasons —
274	    never a silent guess. -/
275	def planMigration (old new : List TableSpec) : Except String MigPlan := do
276	  let mut steps : List MigStep := []
277	  let mut notes : List String := []
278	  -- new and changed tables
279	  for spec in new do
280	    match old.find? (·.name == spec.name) with
281	    | none => steps := steps ++ [.createTable spec]
282	    | some oldSpec =>
283	        if oldSpec == spec then continue
284	        let added := spec.columns.toList.filter fun c =>
285	          (oldSpec.columns.find? (·.name == c.name)).isNone
286	        let dropped := oldSpec.columns.toList.filter fun c =>
287	          (spec.columns.find? (·.name == c.name)).isNone
288	        -- shape changes: additive → restamp, anything else → refused by name
289	        let reshaped := spec.columns.toList.filter fun c =>
290	          match oldSpec.columns.find? (·.name == c.name) with
291	          | some o => o.shape != c.shape
292	          | none => false
293	        for c in reshaped do
294	          if let some o := oldSpec.columns.find? (·.name == c.name) then
295	            shapeChange spec.name c.name o.shape c.shape
296	        -- EnumSet worlds: bit k means variant k, so only a change that keeps
297	        -- every surviving variant at its bit — append, or truncate — is a
298	        -- migration of the data. Anything else silently re-labels stored
299	        -- bits; refused by name.
300	        for c in spec.columns do
301	          if let some o := oldSpec.columns.find? (·.name == c.name) then
302	            if let (some ovs, some nvs) := (o.enumSet, c.enumSet) then
303	              let common := min ovs.size nvs.size
304	              unless ovs.extract 0 common == nvs.extract 0 common do
305	                throw s!"table \"{spec.name}\": EnumSet column \"{c.name}\" changed its variant \
306	order ({ovs} → {nvs}) — stored bits would change meaning. Append or truncate \
307	variants only, or migrate by hand."
308	        -- DDL-level changes, the shape aside
309	        let changed := spec.columns.toList.filter fun c =>
310	          match oldSpec.columns.find? (·.name == c.name) with
311	          | some o => { o with shape := c.shape } != c
312	          | none => false
313	        steps := steps ++ (reshaped.filter fun c => !(changed.any (·.name == c.name))).map
314	          fun c => .restampShape spec.name c.name
315	        for c in added do
316	          unless c.nullable || c.dflt.isSome do
317	            throw s!"table \"{spec.name}\": new column \"{c.name}\" is NOT NULL with no \
318	default — existing rows have no value for it. Make it `Option`, or give it a \
319	`:= default` (existing rows take the default), or migrate by hand."
320	        if changed.isEmpty then
321	          steps := steps ++ added.map (.addColumn spec.name ·)
322	            ++ dropped.map (.dropColumn spec.name ·.name)
323	        else
324	          -- rebuild carries adds and drops along
325	          let copyCols := spec.columns.toList.filterMap fun c =>
326	            if (oldSpec.columns.find? (·.name == c.name)).isSome then some c.name else none
327	          for c in changed do
328	            notes := notes ++ [s!"\"{spec.name}\".\"{c.name}\" changed shape → table rebuild"]
329	          unless dropped.isEmpty do
330	            notes := notes ++ [s!"rebuild of \"{spec.name}\" DROPS columns {dropped.map (·.name)}"]
331	          for c in added do
332	            unless c.nullable || c.dflt.isSome do
333	              throw s!"table \"{spec.name}\": new column \"{c.name}\" must be nullable or \
334	carry a default (rebuild)"
335	          steps := steps ++ [.rebuildTable spec copyCols]
336	  -- dropped tables
337	  for oldSpec in old do
338	    if (new.find? (·.name == oldSpec.name)).isNone then
339	      steps := steps ++ [.dropTable oldSpec.name]
340	  return { steps, notes }
341	
342	/-- Is this plan destructive? dropTable/dropColumn, or a rebuild whose copy
343	    list is shorter than the old table's columns. -/
344	def MigPlan.destructiveAgainst (p : MigPlan) (old : List TableSpec) : Bool :=
345	  p.steps.any fun s =>
346	    s.destructive ||
347	      match s with
348	      | .rebuildTable spec copyCols =>
349	          match old.find? (·.name == spec.name) with
350	          | some o => copyCols.length < o.columns.size
351	          | none => false
352	      | _ => false
353	
354	structure MigrateReport where
355	  applied : List String
356	  notes : List String
357	  fingerprint : String
358	  deriving Repr
359	
360	open Lean (Json) in
361	def MigrateReport.toJson (r : MigrateReport) : Json :=
362	  Json.mkObj [("ok", Json.bool true),
363	    ("applied", Json.arr (r.applied.map Json.str).toArray),
364	    ("notes", Json.arr (r.notes.map Json.str).toArray),
365	    ("fingerprint", Json.str r.fingerprint)]
366	
367	private def readStoredSchema (db : SQLite) : IO (Except String (Option (List TableSpec))) := do
368	  let stmt ← db.prepare "SELECT value FROM _leandb_meta WHERE key = 'schema_json'"
369	  if ← stmt.step then
370	    let raw ← stmt.columnText 0
371	    match Lean.Json.parse raw >>= specsFromJson? with
372	    | .ok specs => return .ok (some specs)
373	    | .error e => return .error s!"stored schema metadata is invalid: {e}"
374	  else
375	    return .ok none
376	
377	private def writeStoredSchema (db : SQLite) (specs : List TableSpec) : IO Unit := do
378	  let stmt ← db.prepare "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO _leandb_meta (key, value) VALUES (?, ?)"
379	  stmt.bindText 1 "schema_json"
380	  stmt.bindText 2 (specsToJson specs).compress
381	  stmt.exec
382	  stmt.reset
383	  stmt.clearBindings
384	  stmt.bindText 1 "schema_fingerprint"
385	  stmt.bindText 2 (fingerprint specs)
386	  stmt.exec
387	
388	/-- Plan (and optionally apply) the migration from an instance's stored
389	    schema to the code's schema. `apply := false` only reports. -/
390	def migrate (path : System.FilePath) (specs : List TableSpec)
391	    (apply : Bool) (allowDestructive : Bool := false) :
392	    IO (Except DbError (Option MigPlan × Option MigrateReport)) := do
393	  if let .error e := validateSchema specs then return .error e
394	  try
395	    let db ← SQLite.open path
396	    db.exec "PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON"
397	    db.exec "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _leandb_meta (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL)"
398	    db.exec migrationsDdl
399	    let old? ← match ← readStoredSchema db with
400	      | .ok old? => pure old?
401	      | .error msg => return .error (.migrate msg)
402	    let old := old?.getD []
403	    match planMigration old specs with
404	    | .error msg => return .error (.migrate msg)
405	    | .ok plan =>
406	        let plan := { plan with isDestructive := plan.destructiveAgainst old }
407	        if plan.steps.isEmpty then
408	          if apply then writeStoredSchema db specs
409	          return .ok (some plan, some ⟨[], ["schema already up to date"], fingerprint specs⟩)
410	        if !apply then
411	          return .ok (some plan, none)
412	        if plan.isDestructive && !allowDestructive then
413	          return .error (.migrate
414	            "plan is destructive (drops tables or columns); pass --allow-destructive")
415	        db.exec "PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF"
416	        db.exec "BEGIN"
417	        try
418	          for step in plan.steps do
419	            for sql in step.sql do
420	              db.exec sql
421	          -- referential integrity must survive the migration
422	          let stmt ← db.prepare "PRAGMA foreign_key_check"
423	          if ← stmt.step then
424	            let t ← stmt.columnText 0
425	            throw <| IO.userError s!"foreign_key_check failed on table {t}"
426	          writeStoredSchema db specs
427	          -- version bump + journal, atomic with the migration itself
428	          let ver := (((← readMeta db "schema_version").bind (·.toNat?)).getD 0) + 1
429	          writeMeta db "schema_version" (toString ver)
430	          let j ← db.prepare
431	            "INSERT INTO _leandb_migrations (steps, fingerprint, ok) VALUES (?, ?, 1)"
432	          j.bindText 1 (Lean.Json.arr
433	            (plan.steps.map (Lean.Json.str ·.describe)).toArray).compress
434	          j.bindText 2 (fingerprint specs)
435	          j.exec
436	          db.exec "COMMIT"
437	        catch e =>
438	          db.exec "ROLLBACK"
439	          db.exec "PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON"
440	          return .error (.migrate (toString e))
441	        db.exec "PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON"
442	        return .ok (some plan, some ⟨plan.steps.map (·.describe), plan.notes, fingerprint specs⟩)
443	  catch e =>
444	    return .error (.sqlite (toString e))
445	
446	/-- What an instance says about itself, readable even when drifted:
447	    (fingerprint, schema_version). `none` = file or meta absent. -/
448	def instanceInfo (path : System.FilePath) : IO (Option (Option String × Option Nat)) := do
449	  if !(← path.pathExists) then return none
450	  try
451	    let db ← SQLite.open path
452	    let fp ← readMeta db "schema_fingerprint"
453	    let ver ← readMeta db "schema_version"
454	    return some (fp, ver.bind (·.toNat?))
455	  catch _ =>
456	    return some (none, none)

module

prelude
public import Std.Async
public import Std.Async.TCP
public import Std.Sync.CancellationToken
public import Std.Sync.Semaphore
public import Std.Http.Server.Config
public import Std.Http.Server.Handler
public import Std.Http.Server.Connection

public section

/-!
# HTTP Server

This module defines a simple, asynchronous HTTP/1.1 server implementation.

It provides the `Std.Http.Server` structure, which encapsulates all server state, and functions for
starting, managing, and gracefully shutting down the server.

The server runs entirely using `Async` and uses a shared `CancellationContext` to signal shutdowns.
Each active client connection is tracked, and the server automatically resolves its shutdown
promise once all connections have closed.
-/

namespace Std.Http
open Std.Async TCP

set_option linter.all true

/--
The `Server` structure holds all state required to manage the lifecycle of an HTTP server, including
connection tracking and shutdown coordination.
-/
structure Server where

  /--
  The context used for shutting down all connections and the server.
  -/
  context : Std.CancellationContext

  /--
  Active HTTP connections
  -/
  activeConnections : Std.Mutex Nat

  /--
  Semaphore used to enforce the maximum number of simultaneous active connections.
  `none` means no connection limit.
  -/
  connectionLimit : Option Std.Semaphore

  /--
  Indicates when the server has successfully shut down.
  -/
  shutdownPromise : Std.Channel Unit

  /--
  Configuration of the server
  -/
  config : Std.Http.Config

  /--
  The local socket address the server is bound to. When `serve` is called with a port of `0`, this
  reflects the ephemeral port assigned by the OS rather than the requested address.
  `none` for servers constructed without an associated listening socket (e.g. `serveConnection`).
  -/
  localAddr : Option Net.SocketAddress := none

namespace Server

/--
Create a new `Server` structure with an optional configuration.
-/

/--
A type class for handling HTTP server requests. Implement this class to define how the server
responds to incoming requests, failures, and `Expect: 100-continue` headers.
-/
class Handler (σ : Type) where
  /--
  Concrete body type produced by `onRequest`.
  Defaults to `Body.Any`, but handlers may override it with any reader/writer-compatible body.
  -/
  ResponseBody : Type := Body.Any

  /--
  Body instance required by the connection loop for receiving response chunks.
  -/
  [responseBodyInstance : Body ResponseBody]

  /--
  Called for each incoming HTTP request.
  -/
  onRequest (self : σ) (request : Request Body.Stream) : ContextAsync (Response ResponseBody)

  /--
  Called when an I/O or transport error occurs while processing a request (e.g. broken socket,
  handler exception). This is a **notification only**: the connection will close regardless of
  the handler's response. Use this for logging and metrics. The default implementation does nothing.
  -/
  onFailure (self : σ) (error : IO.Error) : Async Unit :=
    pure ()

  /--
  Called when a request includes an `Expect: 100-continue` header. Return `true` to send a
  `100 Continue` response and accept the body. If `false` is returned the server sends
  `417 Expectation Failed`, disables keep-alive, and closes the request body reader.
  This function is guarded by `Config.lingeringTimeout` and may be cancelled on server shutdown.
  The default implementation always returns `true`.
  -/
  onContinue (self : σ) (request : Request.Head) : Async Bool :=
    pure true

/--
A stateless HTTP handler.
-/
structure StatelessHandler where
  /--
  Function called for each incoming request.
  -/
  onRequest : Request Body.Stream → ContextAsync (Response Body.Any)

  /--
  Function called when an I/O or transport error occurs. The default does nothing.
  -/
  onFailure : IO.Error → Async Unit := fun _ => pure ()

  /--
  Function called when a request includes `Expect: 100-continue`. Return `true` to accept
  the body or `false` to reject it with `417 Expectation Failed`. The default always accepts.
  -/
  onContinue : Request.Head → Async Bool := fun _ => pure true

instance : Handler StatelessHandler where
  onRequest self request := self.onRequest request
  onFailure self error := self.onFailure error
  onContinue self request := self.onContinue request

namespace Handler

/--
Builds a `StatelessHandler` from a request-handling function.
-/
def ofFn
    (f : Request Body.Stream → ContextAsync (Response Body.Any)) :
    StatelessHandler :=
  { onRequest := f }

/--
Builds a `StatelessHandler` from all three callback functions.
-/
def ofFns
    (onRequest : Request Body.Stream → ContextAsync (Response Body.Any))
    (onFailure : IO.Error → Async Unit := fun _ => pure ())
    (onContinue : Request.Head → Async Bool := fun _ => pure true) :
    StatelessHandler :=
  { onRequest, onFailure, onContinue }

/--
Builds a `StatelessHandler` from a request function and a failure callback. Useful for
attaching error logging to a handler.
-/
def withFailure
    (handler : StatelessHandler)
    (onFailure : IO.Error → Async Unit) :
    StatelessHandler :=
  { handler with onFailure }

Builds a `StatelessHandler` from a request function and a continue callback

I'll design the plan as soon as the explorer notifications land.
